title: Hybrid Evolutionary-Reinforcement Learning Synthesis of Wideband D-Band Three-Port Circuits
authors: İslam Güven, Mehmet Parlak and Dimitri Lederer
summary: Combines evolutionary search, local bit-flip refinement and PPO to synthesize pixelated three-port passive circuits. Full-wave EM simulations guide the search without a precollected training set. D-band divider and balun examples examine simulation cost, gain balance and phase accuracy.

citation.venue: 2026 22nd International Conference on Synthesis, Modeling, Analysis and Simulation Methods, and Applications to Circuits Design (SMACD)

title: World Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Sample-Efficient Wideband Pixelated Passive RF Circuit Synthesis
authors: İslam Güven, Mehmet Parlak and Dimitri Lederer
summary: A learned world model supports policy training between electromagnetic simulations of binary metal layouts. The approach uses imagined rollouts to reduce additional solver calls and evaluates the resulting design search on a wideband directional coupler.

citation.venue: 2026 22nd International Conference on Synthesis, Modeling, Analysis and Simulation Methods, and Applications to Circuits Design (SMACD)

title: Sample-Efficient Trust-Region Discrete Bayesian Optimization for Wideband Multi-Layer Pixelated Passive RF Circuits
authors: İslam Güven, Mehmet Parlak and Dimitri Lederer
summary: Uses a Gaussian-process model in Hamming space and a discrete trust region to search stacked binary metal layouts. Electromagnetic evaluations guide synthesis across different passive circuit types, layer counts and port configurations.

title: Rethinking Microwave Education and Circuit Design Through Machine Learning and Optimization
authors: Mehmet Parlak, İslam Güven and Dimitri Lederer
summary: Proposes teaching microwave circuits through specification-driven electromagnetic synthesis alongside analytical methods. Machine-learning inverse design and multi-objective optimization let students explore beyond predefined topologies while developing intuition about parasitics, process effects and wideband performance.

title: Sustainability-Aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for UAV Response and Monitoring with Joint Communication and Sensing
summary: Studies UAV monitoring policies that jointly choose movement and sensing-communication resources. The environment accounts for batteries, charging and emissions, while detection requires agreement between agents. Experiments compare learned resource allocation with fixed operating configurations.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Time-Critical UAV Medical Supply Delivery with Dynamic Task Allocation
summary: Coordinates UAV deliveries with changing urgency, locations and deadlines under partial information. The study compares PPO-based learning variants using clinic and hospital locations, examining how fleets can adapt task assignments as requests and operating conditions change.

title: AI-Driven Integrated Circuit Design: A Survey of Techniques, Challenges, and Opportunities
authors: İslam Güven, Mehmet Parlak, Dimitri Lederer and Christophe De Vleeschouwer
summary: Reviews AI methods across analog and RFIC topology synthesis, sizing, layout and post-silicon tasks. It compares evolutionary search, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, deep learning and language models, with attention to data efficiency and generalization.

title: Priority-Aware Multi-UAV Search Path Planning with Evolutionary Algorithms and MARL
authors: İslam Güven, Umut İlkbahar, Buse İnç and Evşen Yanmaz
summary: Compares evolutionary planners and multi-agent PPO for missions that balance coverage time, ground-station connectivity and urgent regions. A real-world risk map is used to examine the trade-off between computation cost and adaptive treatment of priority areas.

title: Cooperative Multi-Target Search with UAV Swarms: Evolutionary vs. Reinforcement Learning Strategies
authors: Kadircan Kara, İslam Güven and Evşen Yanmaz
venue: Modeling, Analysis and Simulation of Wireless and Mobile Systems (MSWiM)
summary: Compares evolutionary algorithms with reinforcement learning for cooperative multi-target search by UAV teams. The study considers imperfect sensing and changing information, examining how search policies balance area coverage, network connectivity and revisit timing.

citation.venue: 2025 International Conference on Modeling, Analysis and Simulation of Wireless and Mobile Systems (MSWiM)

title: Sensing-Aware Cooperative Multi-UAV Search with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Develops a cooperative search environment that models uncertain sensing and decentralized information sharing. Multi-agent PPO learns coordinated search policies, with experiments examining performance as the numbers of UAVs and targets change.

title: Adaptive Multi-UAV Coordination for Heterogeneous Target Search and Connect Missions Using Proximal Policy Optimization
Multi-objective path planning for multi-UAV connectivity and area coverage
summary: Plans drone routes while balancing coverage time, connectivity to a ground station and the longest disconnected interval. Evolutionary optimization produces alternative trade-offs instead of a single weighted-sum solution, allowing mission priorities to guide the final choice.

title: Dynamic Multi-UAV Path Planning for Multi-Target Search and Connectivity
authors: Evşen Yanmaz, Hamid Majidi Balanji and İslam Güven
summary: Studies how search and relay UAVs can adapt their routes after discovering targets. Comparing fixed routes, added communication points and active replanning exposes a trade-off between faster detection and maintaining connectivity for timely information delivery.

title: Millimeter-Wave Low Noise Amplifiers in SOI for 5G/6G Joint Communication and Sensing
authors: Mehmet Parlak, Martin Rack, Lucas Nyssens, Théo Denis, Jean-Pierre Raskin and Dimitri Lederer

title: Environmental tests and reliability characterization of pixel-sized colloidal QDs for next-generation display technologies
authors: Mehmet Parlak, H. İ. İlban, K. Karslı, Emre Ünal and Hilmi Volkan Demir
summary: Examines pixel-sized quantum-dot color converters under temperature cycling, thermal shock, humidity and cold exposure. Measurements compare light output and color before and after testing, identifying both thermal resilience and vulnerability to hot, humid conditions.

title: Maintaining Connectivity for Multi-UAV Multi-Target Search Using Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uses multi-agent reinforcement learning for drone search missions that must preserve network connectivity. A convolutional model processes spatial histories and connection states, learning actions through missions with randomized target locations.

title: EV-Integrated Power System Transient Stability Prediction Based on Imaging Time Series and Deep Neural Network
summary: Encodes synchronized voltage measurements as images for a neural network that predicts grid instability. Hybrid simulation supplies realistic training data, and the study compares power-system behavior with and without electric-vehicle fast-charging stations.

title: A Reconfigurable 50-Mb/s–1 Gb/s Pulse Compression Radar Signal Processor With Offset Calibration in 90-nm CMOS
authors: Jun Li, Mehmet Parlak, Hirohito Mukai, Michiaki Matsuo and James F. Buckwalter
venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
summary: Presents a reconfigurable radar signal processor that combines mixed-signal calibration and bandwidth adaptation. The circuit targets improved receiver dynamic range while retaining low-power operation.

title: A Passive I/Q Millimeter-Wave Mixer and Switch in 45-nm CMOS SOI
authors: Mehmet Parlak and James F. Buckwalter
venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
summary: Investigates passive mmWave transmitter and receiver blocks in 45 nm SOI CMOS. Measured SPDT-switch and I/Q-mixer implementations illustrate the technology’s loss and linearity trade-offs.

citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques

title: A 1Gb/s Reconfigurable Pulse Compression Radar Signal Processor in 90nm CMOS
authors: Jun Li, Hirohito Mukai, Mehmet Parlak, Michiaki Matsuo and James F. Buckwalter
summary: Adapts radar processing bandwidth to target range using an analog correlator, a flash converter and a multi-range delay-locked loop. The design implements reconfigurable baseband processing in 90 nm CMOS.

title: Analog Signal Processing for Pulse Compression Radar in 90-nm CMOS
authors: Mehmet Parlak, Michiaki Matsuo and James F. Buckwalter
venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
summary: Implements radar pulse compression in analog baseband circuitry. By exploiting polyphase-code correlation before digitization, the design addresses receiver sensitivity and resolution while reducing demands on converter speed and precision.

citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques

title: A 6-bit Wideband Variable Gain Amplifier with Low Group Delay Variation in 90nm CMOS
authors: Mehmet Parlak, Michiaki Matsuo and James F. Buckwalter
summary: Develops a differential amplifier with 64 gain settings and limited group-delay variation between settings. The design addresses gain control in ranging and positioning receivers, where delay changes can degrade timing accuracy.

title: A 2.5-dB Insertion Loss, DC-60 GHz CMOS SPDT Switch in 45-nm SOI
authors: Mehmet Parlak and James F. Buckwalter
summary: Implements a broadband transmit-receive switch using a series-shunt topology and input-output matching. The study evaluates SOI substrate isolation as part of a low-loss switching design spanning DC through mmWave frequencies.

title: A 2.9-dB Noise Figure, Q-Band Millimeter-Wave CMOS SOI LNA
authors: Mehmet Parlak and James F. Buckwalter
summary: Demonstrates a two-stage cascode LNA in 45 nm SOI CMOS operating across 43–53 GHz. Its matching design addresses noise and input power together, with measurements characterizing gain and noise figure.

title: Bidirectional Circuitry for Millimeter-Wave Pulse Compression Radar
authors: Mehmet Parlak, James F. Buckwalter and Michiaki Matsuo
summary: Combines a bidirectional W-band front end with analog radar preprocessing. Shared amplification, phase shifting and mixing support transmit and receive functions within the same circuit architecture.

title: A Low-Power Dual-Channel Distributed Amplifier for Multielement Receivers
authors: Mehmet Parlak and James F. Buckwalter
venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
summary: Studies a two-channel distributed CMOS amplifier for linear receiver front ends. The analysis relates stage count and cutoff frequency to channel isolation, and examines reverse gain’s effects on noise and intermodulation.

citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques

title: A Low-Power, W-Band Phase Shifter in a 0.12 μm SiGe BiCMOS Process
authors: Mehmet Parlak and James F. Buckwalter
venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Components Letters
summary: Uses a varactor-loaded transmission line for analog phase control. Distributed gain compensates line losses, supporting phase adjustment over the W-band.

citation.venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Components Letters

title: A 77-GHz to 90-GHz Bidirectional Amplifier for Half-Duplex Front-Ends
authors: Joohwa Kim, Mehmet Parlak and James F. Buckwalter
summary: Amplifies waves in either direction using a constructive-wave architecture. The approach removes a separate transmit-receive switch and provides electronic tuning of the operating band.
